chunks.arabic_text: وَبِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ حُصَيْنِ بْنِ عُمَرَ قَالَ

translations.en: And with this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Husayn ibn Amr, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ع إِنَّ الْمُؤْمِنَ أَشَدُّ مِنْ زُبَرِ الْحَدِيدِ إِنَّ الْحَدِيدَ إِذَا أُدْخِلَ النَّارَ تَغَيَّرَ وَ إِنَّ الْمُؤْمِنَ لَوْ قُتِلَ ثُمَّ نُشِرَ ثُمَّ قُتِلَ لَمْ يَتَغَيَّرْ قَلْبُهُ.

translations.en: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The believer is firmer than blocks of iron. Iron, when subjected to fire, changes, but the believer, even if killed, then raised (from death), then killed again, his body cut), then killed again, his heart does not change.

en.summary: In *Sifat al-Shia*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to define the spiritual resilience (*thabat*) of the true believer, contrasting the physical malleability of iron with the immutability of the faithful heart. This metaphor underscores the Shia concept that while worldly trials may test the body, the core of faith (*iman*) remains unshaken, reflecting the divine promise of steadfastness found in the Quranic narrative of the Prophets.
en.seo_question: What is the metaphorical meaning of the believer being firmer than iron?

key_terms.قَلْبُهُ: His heart (symbolizing inner conviction and steadfastness)
